text: The issue of fault is not relevant in determining liability under the tort of Rylands v Fletcher.
Outline the elements of this tort and critically analyse the above statement. [25]
Trespass to the person is no longer necessary as the tort of negligence provides a satisfactory
means of recovery for claimants.
Critically assess this view. [25]
It is unfair to impose liability in tort on one person for the actions of another.
Critically analyse the principle of vicarious liability and consider whether its use is justifiable. [25]
Section B
Tania is training for a marathon and runs in a park which is owned by Barton Town Council. Tania
frequently encounters problems running in the park as the path is in poor condition. She suffers a
wrist injury when she falls due to the uneven surface.
On one of her training runs Tania explores a small track leading into a wooded area of the park.
She runs for a short time and then finds that the track is quite overgrown and it is difficult to run
further. She notices a clearing ahead and climbs over the remains of a fence on to land belonging
to George. She continues her run but breaks her leg when she falls into a well, which has been
inadequately covered.
George had placed a sign stating ‘Danger – Keep Out’ where the track from the park adjoined his
property. However the sign had fallen down and was not visible.
Advise Tania as to her potential claims against Barton Town Council and George. [25]
Alvin is a student musician who converts his garden shed into a recording studio. Lack of money
means that he is unable to soundproof the studio. Alvin often works in the studio until 2am causing
Len, who lives in the adjoining house, to complain.
Alvin ignores Len’s complaints. Len responds by lighting bonfires in his garden whenever Alvin
works late in his studio. The smoke from the bonfires makes it difficult for Alvin to work in the
studio and triggers asthma attacks.
Advise Alvin and Len as to their rights and responsibilities in this situation, and consider what
remedies might be awarded by the court. [25]
Olga is a school teacher. She organises a class trip for 12 students to the local sailing centre
owned and operated by Mike. Having failed to check the weather forecast, Mike gets the students
on to the boat and tells them to remain seated at all times. Once the boat has set sail, one of the
students, Nigel, decides to move up the boat to sit near his friends. He falls and breaks his arm.
The weather becomes stormy and Mike decides to turn back. When the boat is close to shore
it overturns. The students swim to shore, but Nigel struggles in the water because of his injury.
Seeing him in trouble, Olga dives in and rescues him.
Olga has been unable to return to work as she is anxious and experiencing panic attacks.
Advise Olga, Nigel and the other students as to the likely success of an action in negligence
against Mike. [25]
